plan: This auction structure mimics a second-price (Vickrey) auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, regardless of my own bid (as long as it's the highest). In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding above value risks losing money if I win at a high price; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $42.

This auction mechanism effectively functions as a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own sealed bid. In a second-price auction, bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, and bidding my true value ensures I win whenever profitable and never overpay relative to my valuation.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of the ascending clock mechanism. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. My value is $48, so I should bid exactly $48 to ensure I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid, which will always be less than my value.
